Recent bioarchaeological reinterpretation further weakens older captive/non-local assumptions but does not create a new bounded conclusion beyond the already disputed C1 state.

packets.conclusion: Deeper review does not resolve the temporal gap between late ethnographic descriptions of conquered status and the 1700 anchor, nor the conflict with later comparative coding. Oral/Samoan-language evidence remains underrepresented.
packets.gain: No material C1 correction; retrospective-category uncertainty remains the decisive boundary.

packets.conclusion: Stefan Brink's 2021 synthesis materially sharpens the network/territory distinction: Scandinavian actors were major participants in European slave trading, while the social boundary between free and unfree was fluid and labeling Viking-Age Scandinavia as a unitary 'slave society' is probably misleading.
packets.gain: Material inference-boundary improvement: strong slave-trade network participation is explicitly separated from a territorial/societal classification.

new_source.title: Thraldom: A History of Slavery in the Viking Age
new_source.author: Stefan Brink

packets.conclusion: Deeper status-history review materially sharpens the servus/ancilla boundary: the Cluny charters directly evidence transferable/hereditary servile dependence, but medieval Mâconnais scholarship disputes simple equivalence between charter labels, chattel slavery and later serfdom.
packets.gain: Material category/inference improvement: institutional unfreedom is secure while the slavery/serfdom normalization remains explicitly unresolved.

interpretation: Selective C2 remains useful outside polity targets, but only half of these escalations materially improve the compact row. Deep packets should remain triggered rather than universal.
